slides.title: 4 ways to stay off p*rn [[on a long holiday weekend.]]
slides.sub: Thanksgiving, a holiday or just days off — free time is risky time.

slides.title: Fill the [[mornings]]
slides.body: Long weekends start late and lazy — a classic p*rn setup. Plan something before 10 AM every day.

slides.title: Stay [[around people]]
slides.body: Family, friends, a busy café. The more time alone with a screen, the louder the urge.

slides.title: Ways [[3–4]]
items: Beat the food coma. Lying around after big meals can be a trigger — go for a walk.
Keep your sleep close to normal, even on days off.

slides.title: Before the [[weekend]]
items: Write a loose plan for each day.
Keep p*rn blockers on every device you'll use.
Tell someone you'll check in each night.
Pack a book for the downtime.

carousels.name: 6 ways to rebuild your self-image after p*rn (ESRI 64%)

slides.title: 6 ways to rebuild your self-image [[after p*rn.]]
slides.sub: Young men who used p*rn reported a poorer self-image.

slides.title: Of young men [[used it]]
slides.body: In an Irish study of about 4,500 20-year-olds (ESRI, 2024), 64% of young men used online p*rn. Those who did reported lower life satisfaction, more depressive symptoms and a poorer self-image. A link, not proof of cause.

slides.title: Rebuild [[1–3]]
items: Keep tiny promises — self-respect is built in reps.
Train your body for strength, not looks.
Stop comparing yourself to people on screens.

slides.title: Rebuild [[4–6]]
items: Learn something hard and stick with it.
Spend time with people who see the real you.
Talk to yourself like a coach, not a critic.

slides.title: Start [[today]]
items: Pick one from this list.
Do it daily for 7 days.
Stay off p*rn while you do — it feeds the comparison.
Notice how you see yourself by next Monday.

items: Progressive overload. Start small, add a little each week — days without p*rn work the same.
Consistency beats intensity. A steady week beats one heroic day.

slides.title: Lessons [[3–4]]
items: Plateaus are normal. Flat weeks don't mean it's not working.
Rest matters. Tired lifters fail reps. Tired quitters fail too.

slides.title: Lessons [[5–6]]

Form over ego. Do it right, not fast.

slides.title: 5 signs your perfect routine [[is hiding a p*rn problem.]]
slides.sub: Cold plunge at 6. P*rn at midnight.

slides.title: Signs [[1–3]]
items: Your mornings are perfect — your nights aren't.
You track macros but not how often you watch p*rn.
You read about discipline more than you practice it.

slides.title: Signs [[4–5]]
items: You post the gym and hide the late nights.
You feel like a fraud — and work harder to cover it.

slides.title: It's not [[balance]]
slides.body: A great routine doesn't cancel out a p*rn habit. It just makes it easier to ignore. The thing you hide is the thing that needs work.

slides.title: Fix the [[real thing]]
items: Track p*rn as honestly as your workouts.
Build a night routine as strong as your morning one.
Tell your gym partner or a friend.
Make quitting p*rn your main goal for 30 days.
